title: Scaling by Diversified Experience for Vision-Language-Action Models
claim: A decoupling mechanism keeps only control-relevant features for action, yielding strong robot performance while preserving multimodal reasoning ability.
layout: Top method diagram with legend; bottom row of three panels with dashed dividers
description: The figure is a banner with two tiers. The top-left shows the large blue title 'SyVLA' with the tagline 'Among the first open-source VLAs with Visual-Language Reasoning'. The top-right is a pipeline sketch. A VLM bar takes the instruction 'Fold the shirt.', an image, and a row of blue Feature Query Tokens. It emits the text '<reason>I should fold it in half.</reason>' and a row of green tokens, with one orange token marking control-irrelevant information. A red 'Intention Decoupling' arrow leads to a second row where the orange token is hatched as masked. That row feeds an Action Expert bar, which also takes an image and the robot state q_t, and outputs the action chunk {a_t ... a_t+T}. A legend lists control related (green), control irrelevant (orange) and masked (hatched). The bottom row has three panels. caption: We propose an Intention Decoupling algorithm to disentangle control-irrelevant high-level reasoning information in Feature Query Tokens, and develop an RL pipeline for stable real-world reinforcement learning. With these two methods, our SyVLA model achieves a balance between robotic task competence and visual-language understanding capability preservation.
abstract: Vision-Language-Action models face significant challenges in real-world deployment due to the entanglement of high-level reasoning with low-level control, and the instability of policy optimization. In this paper, we introduce SyVLA, a robust VLA model trained with diversified experiences. We propose an Intention Decoupling algorithm to isolate control-relevant features from reasoning contexts and a similar-sample guided RL pipeline to stabilize policy updates and mitigate distribution shift. Extensive experiments on real-world robotic tasks and multi-modal benchmarks demonstrate that SyVLA achieves superior task success rates and stronger out-of-distribution generalization compared to existing methods, while effectively preserving core vision-language capabilities. Codes and Datasets is released on \href{https://sy-vla.github.io/}{project page}.
